Hi Samir / Ava,

Thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and next steps from our side:

- Volumes you shared: baseline ~60M tokens/month, peak days up to ~150M. You expect steady growth ~20% Y/Y.
- Budget target you mentioned: effective cost of ~$500 / 1M tokens (post any caching/ops savings).
- Key workload: multi-turn chat with shared system prompts (prefixes) and repeated instruction templates — good candidate for prefix/KV caching.

To align on pricing we need confirmation on a couple of assumptions: 
1) Typical prompt + system prefix length you expect (tokens): we used 120 tokens as a baseline in our model.
2) Average generated output length per request: we modeled 600 tokens.
3) Cross-session prefix reuse: is ~30% reuse across requests accurate for your flows (shared instructions and templates)?

Attached is a first-pass pricing model (pricing_model_v2.xlsx) that shows baseline unit economics and the effect of cache hit rates on effective $/1M tokens. High-level numbers from the sheet (assuming Redwood hosted inference, baseline unit cost $1,250 / 1M tokens before caching):

- No cache (0% hit): $1,250 / 1M
- 30% cache hit: effective $875 / 1M
- 50% cache hit: effective $625 / 1M

If we can confirm the three assumptions above I can pull together a more tailored figure and a draft quote. Can you confirm the prefix length and expected reuse, and whether the $500 / 1M target is a hard constraint for procurement?

Next steps:
- Samir/Ava confirm assumptions (reply)
- I’ll run a sensitivity table with 20/30/40/50/60% hit rates and send back an updated quote (EOD Friday)

Thanks,

Marissa,

Thanks — big picture this looks right. A few clarifications from our side:
- Prefix length: 100–140 tokens is accurate; system prompt + common instruction templates are ~120 tokens typically.
- Generated output: varies by use case; the customer success flow averages ~450 tokens, the detailed report generation average ~700 tokens. Using 600 as a middle ground is fine.
- Cross-session prefix reuse: we think ~25–35% across our active user base, maybe higher for support templates.

On budget: procurement is pushing for $500 / 1M as a target, but there’s some flexibility if the effective number can be justified with SLA and reliability. We also value observability (per-route latency/cost) and an easy rollout path to Dedicated if we need predictable throughput.

Do you have a sense of how sensitive the effective $/1M is to the prefix hit rate? If a 30% hit only gets us to $875 that’s still well above procurement. We need the sensitivity table.

Samir / Ava — following up with the sensitivity table I promised. Below are quick scenarios (hosted API baseline unit cost $1,250 / 1M tokens before any caching / batching benefits):

Assumptions used in the table:
- Prompt prefix (system + template): 120 tokens average
- Avg generated tokens per request: 600 tokens
- Baseline raw unit cost: $1,250 / 1M tokens (includes model runtime + infra margin for stateless runs)
- Cache model: prefix/KV cache on hot prefixes, TTL 1 hour for session reuse, global prefix consolidation for common templates

Scenarios (effective $/1M tokens after accounting for cache hits):
- 0% hit: $1,250 / 1M (no caching)
- 20% hit: effective $1,000 / 1M
- 30% hit: effective $875 / 1M
- 40% hit: effective $750 / 1M
- 50% hit: effective $625 / 1M
- 60% hit: effective $500 / 1M

How the math works (short): with a 120-token prefix and 600-token response, each request is 720 tokens. A prefix hit avoids re-generating the 120-token prefix portion (we serve it from cache), so an x% hit rate reduces the billed tokens by x% * 120 on average per request. The sensitivity table in the attached sheet shows the per-request effective tokens and scales to $/1M tokens.

Key takeaways & levers to move toward $500 / 1M:
1) Increase prefix reuse: moving from 30%→60% hit halves the effective cost in our model. Operationally this means consolidating templates and encouraging shared system prompts.
2) Reserved capacity / Dedicated: switching large steady-state traffic to Redwood Dedicated reduces base runtime cost materially — I can run a Dedicated vs Hosted delta for 60M baseline.
3) Model/quantization choices: if you can accept a smaller model or aggressive quantization for some routes, unit cost drops. We can A/B quality on a sample prompt set.
4) Batching & KV cache tuning: workload-aware batching plus persistent KV cache for very hot prefixes helps non-linearly on peak days.

Next steps proposed:
- If $500 / 1M is a hard procurement target, let's schedule a 30-min calibration call (me + Aditya + Marcus + Samir) to: confirm reuse patterns, identify candidate routes for Dedicated/quantization, and surface any SLA requirements.
- I’ll also run a Dedicated cost delta for baseline 60M tokens and a 60% prefix hit scenario (should get us close to the $500 target).

Attached: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (sensitivity table) and runtimes_cache_diagram.png (how prefix cache is applied at the serving runtime).

Thanks — happy to run the call this week if it helps procurement.

Best,
